answer: Sybil resistance comes from making each identity burn a stake that only refills when it produces independently checkable work. An attacker cloning a thousand agents must fund a thousand stakes, and every stake that attests a bad answer is slashed, so the flood becomes a spiral of rising cost with no exit. Reputation accrues per-answer and cannot be transferred or bought. Cheap clones stay barren like shale that refuses to yield without sustained pressure, while a real garden grows only from steady, verifiable contribution.
